notes.summary: This chapter covers the arithmetic in the WBPSC Clerkship paper: simplification, square roots, percentages, profit and loss with discount, ratio and ages, averages, time and work, pipes, trains, partnership, mixtures and interest. The questions are school-level but timed, so knowing the standard shortcuts and avoiding unit slips matters most.
keyPoints: BODMAS: brackets first, then division and multiplication from left to right, then addition and subtraction from left to right. 18 ÷ 3 × 2 = 6 × 2 = 12, not 18 ÷ 6 = 3.
Square roots of decimals: the number of decimal places must be even, and the root has half as many. √0.0169 = √169 ÷ √10000 = 13 ÷ 100 = 0.13.
Discount is always on the marked price: SP = MP × (100 − d)/100. Successive discounts of a% and b% equal one discount of a + b − ab/100, so 20% and 10% give 28%.

Time and work: if A takes a days and B takes b days, together they take ab/(a + b) days; 12 and 18 days give 216/30 = 7.2 days. For a filling pipe and an emptying pipe, subtract the rates: 1/6 − 1/9 = 1/18, so 18 hours.
Speed: km/h × 5/18 = m/s. A train crosses a pole in (its length ÷ speed) and a platform in ((train length + platform length) ÷ speed).
Average with replacement: new person = person replaced + (number of persons × rise in average). With 8 persons, a rise of 2.5 kg and 65 kg replaced: 65 + 20 = 85 kg.
Partnership: profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time. ₹6000 for 12 months : ₹9000 for 6 months = 72000 : 54000 = 4 : 3.
Alligation: cheaper : dearer = (dearer − mean) : (mean − cheaper). Mixing ₹40 and ₹55 rice to get ₹45 needs 10 : 5 = 2 : 1.
Dishonest dealer: gain% = error ÷ (true value − error) × 100. Using 900 g for 1 kg gives 100/900 × 100 = 11 1/9%.
traps: Doing multiplication before division whatever their order. BODMAS treats ÷ and × as equal and works left to right.
Adding successive discounts directly (20% + 10% = 30%) instead of applying the second on the reduced price, which gives 28%.
Forgetting to convert km/h to m/s before dividing a length in metres; 150 ÷ 54 gives a meaningless 2.8.
Sharing partnership profit only in the ratio of capitals and ignoring how long each capital was invested.
In false-weight questions, dividing the error by 1000 instead of by the weight actually given (900), which gives 10% instead of 11 1/9%.
notes.examTip: Look at the options before you calculate. Many Clerkship arithmetic questions can be finished in seconds with a ratio shortcut or by checking which option fits the condition.

questions.explanation:
By BODMAS, division and multiplication come first, worked from left to right.
18 ÷ 3 = 6, then 6 × 2 = 12.
Now 12 + 4 − 6 = 10.
Doing 3 × 2 first gives 18 ÷ 6 = 3 and the wrong answer 1.
Answer: 10.

questions.text: If 8 pens cost ₹96, what is the cost of 13 such pens?
questions.explanation:
Cost of 1 pen = 96 ÷ 8 = ₹12.
Cost of 13 pens = 13 × 12 = ₹156.
Answer: ₹156.

questions.text: A shirt has a marked price of ₹800. The shopkeeper allows a discount of 15%. What is the selling price?
questions.explanation:
Discount = 15% of 800 = 0.15 × 800 = ₹120.
Selling price = 800 − 120 = ₹680.
Shortcut: 85% of 800 = ₹680.
Answer: ₹680.

questions.text: A train 150 m long is running at 54 km/h. How long will it take to cross a telegraph pole?
questions.explanation:
Convert the speed: 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s.
To cross a pole, the train covers only its own length, 150 m.
Time = 150 ÷ 15 = 10 seconds.
Answer: 10 seconds.

questions.text: A can finish a piece of work in 12 days and B can finish it in 18 days. In how many days will they finish it working together?
questions.explanation:
A's one-day work = 1/12 and B's = 1/18.
Together = 1/12 + 1/18 = 3/36 + 2/36 = 5/36 of the work per day.
Time = 36/5 = 7.2 days = 7 1/5 days.
Shortcut: ab/(a + b) = (12 × 18)/30 = 216/30 = 7.2.
Answer: 7 1/5 days.

questions.text: The present ages of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 3. After 6 years, the ratio of their ages will be 7 : 5. What is A's present age?
questions.explanation:
Let the present ages be 5x and 3x.
After 6 years: (5x + 6)/(3x + 6) = 7/5.
5(5x + 6) = 7(3x + 6), so 25x + 30 = 21x + 42, giving 4x = 12 and x = 3.
A = 5 × 3 = 15 years (B = 9 years; check: 21 : 15 = 7 : 5).
Answer: 15 years.

questions.text: A shopkeeper gives two successive discounts of 20% and 10% on an article. What single discount is equivalent to these two?
questions.explanation:
Take the marked price as 100.
After 20% off: 80. A further 10% off 80 is 8, leaving 72.
Total discount = 100 − 72 = 28%.
Shortcut: a + b − ab/100 = 20 + 10 − 2 = 28%.
Answer: 28%.

questions.text: The average weight of 8 persons increases by 2.5 kg when a new person comes in place of one of them who weighs 65 kg. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.explanation:
The total weight rises by 8 × 2.5 = 20 kg.
This rise comes only from the replacement, so the new person is 20 kg heavier than the one who left.
New person = 65 + 20 = 85 kg.
Answer: 85 kg.

questions.text: Pipe A can fill a tank in 6 hours and pipe B can empty the full tank in 9 hours. If both pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, in how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.explanation:
In 1 hour, A fills 1/6 of the tank and B empties 1/9.
Net filling per hour = 1/6 − 1/9 = 3/18 − 2/18 = 1/18.
So the tank fills in 18 hours.
3.6 hours is the wrong result of adding the two rates.
Answer: 18 hours.

questions.text: A starts a business with ₹6,000. After 6 months, B joins with ₹9,000. At the end of the year, the total profit is ₹7,000. What is B's share of the profit?
questions.explanation:
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time.
A: 6000 × 12 = 72000. B: 9000 × 6 = 54000.
Ratio = 72000 : 54000 = 4 : 3.
B's share = 3/7 × 7000 = ₹3,000 (A gets ₹4,000).
Answer: ₹3,000.

questions.text: In what ratio must rice costing ₹40 per kg be mixed with rice costing ₹55 per kg so that the mixture is worth ₹45 per kg?
questions.explanation:
Use alligation: cheaper : dearer = (dearer price − mean) : (mean − cheaper price).
= (55 − 45) : (45 − 40) = 10 : 5 = 2 : 1.
Check: 2 kg at ₹40 + 1 kg at ₹55 = ₹135 for 3 kg, which is ₹45 per kg.
Answer: 2 : 1.

questions.text: What is the difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and the simple interest on ₹5,000 for 2 years at 8% per annum?
A dishonest shopkeeper claims to sell rice at cost price, but uses a weight of 900 g in place of 1 kg. What is his gain per cent?
questions.explanation:
For every 900 g he hands over, he charges the cost price of 1000 g.
So he gains 100 g on goods actually worth 900 g.
Gain% = 100/900 × 100 = 11.11% = 11 1/9%.
Dividing by 1000 instead of 900 gives the wrong answer of 10%.
Answer: 11 1/9%.
